headline: Argentina's Country Risk Surpasses 900 Points as Default Insurance Costs Hit One-Year High
summary: Argentina's country risk indicator climbed above 900 points, while two-year credit default swaps reached 972 basis points—their highest level in a year—driven by external shocks and internal doubts over economic program sustainability.
why: Sovereign risk metrics and credit default swaps reflect investor confidence in a government's ability to service its debt obligations and maintain macroeconomic stabilization programs.

impacts.name: Argentina Credit Default Swap
impacts.why: Rising sovereign default insurance costs directly measure growing perceived risk of non-payment.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Uncertainty surrounding domestic economic policies and external financial shocks stoked investor doubts, pushing sovereign debt insurance costs and risk indicators to annual highs.
